title: Publishing: Teddy McRae and the 1939 Jubilee Swing royalty
summary: Hammond's circle teach him to publish his own tunes, and in 1981 he gets a small London royalty for Jubilee Swing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yeah, and it was a big seller. He had this magazine, what they were saying about it and they said they had to leave but they would try their best to get one of those, because I don't know how mine got away--I did have a few, (inaudible) I didn't have a publisher to protect it. Now to show you what it meant by bootleg things sometimes, I tried to talk to some of these youngsters when they say they're going to make a record; I'll say one thing about Teddy McRae, I met him in 1939--is it McRae or McVey?

McRae, yeah; Teddy McRae. When we recorded, they did a number for Hammond and the first thing he said is Ernie, what publisher you going to put this with? Anyway, he opened my eyes on how to do that and we did that, and believe it or not, this is eighty one, and I believe last June I

got a check on one of the numbers, Jubilee Swing, that I did in 1939 from Europe, from London; it wasn't much but it goes to show you when anything is done right what it means. I think it was a dollar and eighty one cents or something.
